title: Which one is banana man? Evaluating vision-language models in multi-turn pragmatic interpretation
abstract: arXiv:2608.29571v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Flexible adaptation to context and shared pragmatic intuitions contribute to smooth human conversation. Iterated reference games---in which players repeatedly pick out novel referents using language---present a test case for agents' ability to perform context-sensitive pragmatic reasoning in multi-turn linguistic environments. We tested humans and vision--language models on their ability to identify the intended meaning of descriptions produced in iterated reference games, varying the provided context in terms of amount, order, and relevance. While humans performed well consistently, the models we evaluated could make use of prior context to interpret humans' referring expressions, but they struggled to build up the relevant context to interpret those expressions effectively. Our results suggest that the models we evaluated lack core skills needed for efficient linguistic collaboration.

translated_title: 谁是香蕉人？评估视觉-语言模型在多轮语用理解中的表现
translated_abstract: 对语境的灵活适应和共享的语用直觉有助于人类对话的顺畅进行。迭代指称游戏——即参与者反复使用语言来指认新异对象——为测试智能体在多轮语言环境中进行语境敏感的语用推理能力提供了一个测试场景。我们测试了人类和视觉-语言模型在迭代指称游戏中识别描述所表达意图的能力，并在数量、顺序和相关性方面改变所提供的语境。虽然人类始终表现良好，但我们评估的模型虽然能够利用先前的语境来解释人类的指称表达，却难以自行构建相关语境以有效理解这些表达。我们的结果表明，我们所评估的模型缺乏进行高效语言协作所需的核心技能。
tldr: 研究发现，视觉-语言模型虽能利用已有语境理解人类的指称表达，却难以自行构建相关语境，缺乏高效语言协作所需的核心语用推理能力。
en_tdlr: Vision-language models can use prior context to interpret human referring expressions but struggle to build up relevant context themselves, suggesting they lack core skills needed for efficient linguistic collaboration.
